title: Rick Explains Firewalls vs IDS: Cybersecurity Battle!
caption: Firewall vs IDS—who’s your cybersecurity BFF? 🔥 #CyberSecurity

scenes.script: Alright, Morty! You ever wonder what actually stops those evil hackers from stealing your mom's Wi-Fi password?
scenes.web_image: cartoon hacker trying to steal data

scenes.script: Uh, yeah? Is it the little box that goes beep when I try to watch Netflix in 4K?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty with a dumb looking without understanding.png

scenes.script: Close enough! That box is your firewall, Morty. It checks if traffic is allowed or not based on rules.
scenes.web_image: network traffic diagram with green and red arrows

scenes.script: So it’s like the bouncer at a club, right? ‘No shirt, no shoes, no service’—but for data packets!
scenes.web_image: bouncer checking ID at club entrance

scenes.script: Exactly! Now, the Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is like a spy watching the party. It flags shady behavior but doesn’t kick anyone out.
scenes.web_image: detective with magnifying glass observing people

scenes.script: So if someone’s wearing a fake mustache, the IDS is like, ‘Hey, that guy looks suspicious!’ but doesn’t stop him?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty looking to another side without caring.png
scenes.web_image: person in disguise at a party

scenes.script: Precisely! Now, the Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) is like security that tackles the guy with the fake mustache before he steals the punch bowl.
So, firewall blocks bad data at the door, IDS yells ‘hey!’ if something weird’s happening inside, and IPS stops it before it causes chaos?
Bingo! And sometimes, modern firewalls combine all three because even IPS needs a nap occasionally.
So if my Wi-Fi gets hacked, is it because the bouncer let someone in or the spy fell asleep on the job?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty evil with a serious looking and a portal gun.png

scenes.script: Usually both, Morty. That’s why you need all three—like the Three Stooges of cybersecurity!
Got it! So, in real life, if my bank’s website gets hacked, that’s a job for the IPS?
Exactly! The firewall stops obvious junk, IDS spots the sneaky stuff, and IPS smacks it down. Just like how your mom’s cooking keeps me alive despite my liver problems!
scenes.web_image: medical scan of a damaged liver

topic: What is the difference between a firewall and a intrusion detection system?
